name: NGW World Title
notes: The full reign ledger is served at /promotions/ngw/archive/world-title-history.html and /promotions/ngw/archive/champions-and-title-history-2004-11.html; it is not yet transcribed into this registry.
epitaph: Crowned at NGW's first pay-per-view, Out Cold I on 25 February 2000, when Excalibur beat Chris Jericho in a no-disqualification steel cage match, and vacated four days later when the man who took it off him quit. The fed's own ledger runs the belt through thirty-six numbered reigns; Scottywood's own is the longest thing on it, seven defences deep through the spring of 2000, and Scott King was carrying it when the fed last published a title page in November 2004.

name: NGW Xtreme Title
notes: The full reign ledger, built from /promotions/ngw/archive/xtreme-title-history.html and cross-checked against /promotions/ngw/archive/champions-and-title-history-2004-11.html, is transcribed into this registry.
epitaph: Made as the NGW Cage Title and renamed on 6 April 2000, and it kept the shape of the first name: its own ledger is a run of Hell in a Cell, graveyard, buried alive, anarchy and mega mall brawl matches, fifty numbered reigns deep. Perry Saturn won the first one out of a triple Hell in a Cell with the belt hung from the roof of the third cage; John Hitchin broke the fed's own title-reign record holding it in July 2004, and it was vacant when the last title page went up that November.

name: NGW Tag Team Titles

epitaph: Thirty-three numbered reigns from January 2000, and twice inside the first year they changed hands without a tag match: once on the stipulation of a six-man at Xtrememania I, and once when Rey Jr. simply gave his half of them to Triple H. Vacant on the fed's own last title page.

name: NGW American Title
notes: The full reign ledger, built from /promotions/ngw/archive/american-title-history.html and cross-checked against /promotions/ngw/archive/champions-and-title-history-2004-11.html, is transcribed into this registry.
epitaph: Won first out of a seven-man battle royal by one of the fed's own founders four days after it opened, vacated a week later, and carried through thirty-five more reigns. It was vacated again in August 2003 after John Hitchin was written into a limo accident, and Pr0t0typ3 — later fired and put on the fed's own public blacklist — was holding it when the last title page went up.

name: NGW Battle Dome Title
notes: The reign ledger is served at /promotions/ngw/archive/battle-dome-title-history.html; it is not yet transcribed into this registry.
epitaph: The belt the fed's own thirty-man Battle Dome match played for, and Time Bomb was carrying it at the last title page. Border Line 2004 ended with the referee handing it to John Hitchin on the turnbuckles.

name: NGW Untamed Title
notes: The full reign ledger, built from /promotions/ngw/archive/untamed-title-history.html, is transcribed into this registry. The belt is listed on the fed's own retired-titles page (/promotions/ngw/archive/retired-titles-2004-09.html) despite a 2004 revival under 24/7 rule the dedicated ledger itself records.
epitaph: Created by Brian Hardy on 15 May 2000 and awarded to Brian Hardy by Brian Hardy the same day, and defended in hardcore matches almost exclusively for the rest of its life. Fifty-seven numbered reigns, one of them vacated with the note "Title Vacated when the site was deleted"; the fed retired the belt.
